title: [Snappi] ports selection will not work if pre-configured portchannel or vlans are used for multi-dut test.
author: amitpawar12
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

The function "setup_dut_ports" does the following:
- Checks for the VLAN interfaces for the test and increments port_config_list in the process.
- Checks for portchannel interfaces on the DUT and increments port_config_list.
- If multidut:
     - Configures P2P ip-address on the DUT in 20.x.x.x network.
 - else:
     - Checks for L3 interfaces (router interfaces on DUT).

Issue:
- This function does not check the length of port_config_list and proceeds in the order given above. 
- So an example, if the portchannel interfaces are present on the DUT and snappi_ports has also those ports, then port_config_list will be populated.
- It will check for multi-dut and for multi-DUT, it will still go ahead and try to configure p2p interfaces on the DUT portchannel interfaces. This will cause failure. 

 

### Steps to Reproduce

- Have preconfigured port-channels via minigraph.
- Run any snappi_tests on multi-dut.
- This should work on single-DUT because single-DUT else statement prioritizes L3 interface config which does not configure anything  and ONLY uses router interfaces on DUT.



### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior:
The p2p IP-addresses are attempted to be configured on the DUT port-channel interfaces.

Expected behavior:
- After each iteration, there should be check to see the size of port_config_list and snappi_ports are same.
- L3 interfaces should be prioritized over p2p IP address interface config.
- If no L3 interface is present, then p2p IP address should select ports which are not portchannels or vlans.

Existing snappi setup_dut_port:

Code looks for VLANs, continues to look for port-channels for the test.
Based on whether dut is multi-dut, it will try to configure P2P IPs (in 20.x.x.x network) for multi-DUT or use router interfaces in case of single-DUT.
Drawbacks:

This is done irrespective of the SETUP flag being passed as TRUE or FALSE.
This is a problem, when test selects combination of port-channels and router interfaces. Lets say, there is port-channel interface A and router-interface B used for the test.
Test selects port-channel from the minigraph and assigns it to the test. However, for multi-DUT, code then tries to configure P2P IPs on (20.x.x.x) on both interface A and B by function '__intf_config_multidut'. This will work for interface B but won't work for interface A and test will FAIL.
If the test intends to use all ports as port-channels, the code will still try to configure p2p IPs on the DUT, which is not required.
When SETUP flag is False and same function is called for clean-up, although test could be using port-channel, function '__intf_config_multidut' will be still called and will try to remove non-existent 20.x.x.x IPs from the interfaces.

Summary:
Fixes #22392 

### Type of change

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The motivation of the PR is to improve the port-selection logic in setup_dut_ports.

Test will look for snappi_ports which are configued as VLANs, port-channels, Router Interfaces and then P2P interfaces in that order. The significance of snappi_ports is still the same and test will look for snappi_ports which are present in the above order.

#### How did you do it?
- Additionally enumerated Router interfaces and MacsecInterfaces in common/snappi_tests/ports.py.
- Test has identified snappi_ports as Rx and Tx interfaces.
- If setup flag is True, test will look if these ports are VLAN interface/s, port-channel interface/s, router interface/s and p2p IP interfaces in that order.
- With setup=True, if port defined in snappi_ports are VLANs, then test will return these ports without checking further. If not, it will check if these 2 ports are port-channels and will return them if they both are port-channels. This continues for router-interface and then p2p interface.
- If setup flag is False, then port-channel and VLAN interface checks are skipped as there is no 'explicit' configuration on the DUT for them.
- If setup flag is False, then test checks if interface type is Router interface or p2p Interface and calls appropriate function for clean-up.
- Test is prioritizing Router interfaces (IP interfaces already configured on DUT and defined as snappi_ports) over p2p IP interfaces.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Tested on local master branch with multi-DUT scenarios.

Scenario#1 - All ports as port-channel.
Scenario#2 - One port-channel interface and other router interface( __l3_intf_config).
Code selects the static ports from variables.override.yml file and checking if they are VLANs, port-channels, router interfaces and p2p interfaces and using them accordingly.

comments.author: amitpawar12
comments.body:
> Thanks for the fix. One concern: when setup=True, the VLAN/portchannel checks share the same port_config_list. If only a subset of snappi_ports are VLANs, __vlan_intf_config will append entries, found_ports() is false, and then __portchannel_intf_config can append more, resulting in mixed types even though the intent says ‘both ports are VLANs/port-channels’. Consider clearing/isolating port_config_list between attempts or explicitly verifying all snappi_ports match the type before returning.
**[Amit]** One of the current limitations of the snappi_test is to support mixed type of interfaces for testing. The Rx and Tx ports for the test are coming from variables.override.yml file. If a user wants to have one of the ports as port-channel and other as VLAN port, then user just has to define them in the above file. The above code will search and use the minigraph to find these ports and use them for test (as port-channel and VLANs). 
If these ports are configured entirely as one of the types (VLANs, port-channels, or router interfaces), test will use them as is. The flexibility lies with the user how the ports are defined in the minigraph and test will just pick them as is.

\n\nMinor: pytest_assert messages use 'Failed to configure via {fn.**name**}' without an f-string, so it will print literally; consider f'Failed ...'.\n\nAI agent on behalf of Ying.
**[Amit]** I have fixed and tested this by explicitly returning FALSE from one of the functions and check the error message.

Additionally, I have also fixed the logic for cleanup when setup=False. Code will iterate through the code to find type of interface and will call appropriate function for cleanup with setup=False flag.

Thanks for the comments @yxieca
